title: ZITADEL as an OpenID Connect Provider for Casdoor
headline: Sign in to Casdoor with ZITADEL
summary: Add ZITADEL to Casdoor as an OpenID Connect provider, self-hosted or ZITADEL Cloud, and people sign in to your Casdoor applications with their ZITADEL accounts.

steps.title: Create a web application
steps.text: In the ZITADEL Console, open the project the application belongs to (or create one), click **New** under its applications and choose **Web**.

steps.title: Choose Code and add the redirect URI
steps.text: Pick the **Code** authentication method: Casdoor sends the client secret with HTTP Basic authentication, which is what Code expects. Then add the redirect URI:

steps.title: Copy the credentials
steps.text: Create the application. ZITADEL shows the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** once, so copy both now.

tips: ZITADEL's `preferred_username` is the login name, such as `alice@acme.zitadel.cloud`, and Casdoor uses it as the username of new users. Set a user mapping for `username` in Casdoor if you want something else.
ZITADEL only accepts plain-http redirect URIs in Development mode, so use https for Casdoor.

faqs.question: Do I need User Info inside ID Token?
faqs.answer: No. Casdoor also calls ZITADEL's userinfo endpoint, which returns the name and email.

faqs.question: Can I use the PKCE authentication method instead?
faqs.answer: That method issues no client secret, while Casdoor's provider is a confidential client. Use Code; Casdoor sends a PKCE challenge on top of the secret anyway.
